title: Candidate effectors of two Mucor strains isolated from Marchantia
text:
What this is



A working analysis, not a finished study. Every candidate here is a prediction from sequence and structure; none has been expressed or assayed. Section 10 of the report states the limitations explicitly, and the section headed Upstream issues found records problems located in reference data rather than in this analysis.
The source of truth is analysis/mucor_secretome/ in the repository; this page renders REPORT.md from that directory, so the two cannot drift.
Status: in progress. Last updated 2026-11-12. Code: analysis/mucor_secretome/. All analysis ran on the UCR HPCC.

title: Candidate effectors of two Mucor strains isolated from Marchantia
text:
The question
Two Mucor strains, JEM1 and JEM2, were isolated from Marchantia (MorenoLab, shared/projects/MorenoLab/Mucor_genomes). The practical questions are:

Which of their secreted proteins are candidate effectors?
Could any of them interact with host proteins?

Species identity was a secondary question that turned out to matter, because it determines which genomes count as “relatives” when measuring how lineage-restricted a candidate is.

Two bugs had to be fixed before this ran at all:

ITSx found no ITS in any of the four assemblies, controls included: the rDNA array is collapsed or broken in all of them. The MorenoLab ITSx result that an earlier version of this analysis would have fallen back on is not ITS either — JEM1’s “full” sequence is SSU, reported with a negative ITS length. The method was changed to blast every Mucoromycota UNITE reference against each assembly, which needs no intact ITS.

8. Why the chitin axis
Mucorales cell walls are chitin and chitosan. In M. paleacea, the LysM pair MpaLYR/MpaCERK1 discriminates symbiosis from immunity by chitin-oligomer length — CO7 triggers immunity, CO4 activates symbiosis genes (Cell 2025). In M. polymorpha, chitin and peptidoglycan are the patterns that trigger a ROS burst while other MAMPs do not (Curr Biol 2023).
That makes a mechanistic screen rather than a fishing expedition:

9. The AlphaFold 3 screen
Two panels, both complete: 196 chitin-panel jobs (128 fungal × host pairs, 32 pairs involving a control chain, 36 ligand runs) and 426 monomers of the set ESMFold could not fold. MSAs were computed once per chain and reused.

9.1 Where the threshold comes from
iPTM has no universal cut, and the AlphaFold-Multimer figures (> 0.8 confident, < 0.6 likely wrong) were calibrated on large complexes, not small cysteine-rich effectors. So the cut is taken from this run’s own controls and its own background.

The negative control (0.13) sits just below the median of the panel’s own background (0.16), which is the result that makes the rest interpretable: the screen’s bulk behaviour is the no-interaction case, so the background is a usable empirical null rather than an assumption.

9.3 A control that argues against two of the five
The AtCERK1 LysM ectodomain (4EBZ) was included as a ligand-binding positive. Paired instead with a Marchantia LysM receptor it scores 0.84 — higher than any fungal candidate in the panel.
Both chains are LysM domains, and neither is the other’s effector. That puts a number on how much iPTM “LysM meeting LysM” earns on fold compatibility alone, and it is more than any result in §9.2. The chitinase-domain and deacetylase hits are not explained by it, though both are chitin-binding proteins paired with chitin-binding receptors, which is a weaker version of the same concern.
This control was not planned for this purpose — it fell out of the cross-pairing — and it is the most informative single row in the table.

title: Candidate effectors of two Mucor strains isolated from Marchantia
text:
10. Limitations

No expression data. Every candidate is a prediction from sequence and structure; none is known to be expressed in planta.
Structure prediction is prioritisation, not evidence of interaction. A confident fold says what a protein resembles. A confident iPTM says two chains can be modelled together. Neither is a binding assay.
JEM1’s lineage restriction is confounded with species sampling (§5).
The Marchantia panel counts are not normalised (§7), and assert no orthology.
The host species of the isolates is unrecorded, so both liverworts are treated symmetrically; knowing it would let them be weighted.
ESMFold’s low-pLDDT models are ambiguous. Low confidence may mean prediction failure or genuine disorder — small, cysteine-rich, secreted and unstructured-until-bound is a real effector phenotype. The AF3 re-run (§9.5) separates them for 76 of 426; the remaining ~70 % stay ambiguous.
The AF3 screen ranks candidates; it does not identify interactions. Nothing in the panel reaches the positive control, one candidate rests on replication across three receptors rather than on its score, and §9.3 shows that chitin-binding domains paired with chitin-binding receptors score well without any interaction being implied. These are proteins worth assaying, in an order; they are not findings.
Fold calls come from the transformers ESMFold backend (§6 note), which differs from the original fair-esm run for 18 of 559 proteins, nearly all at the pLDDT 70 boundary. The cerato-platanin call sits at 72.0, two points above that cutoff — it is threshold-fragile and should not be quoted as settled.

12. Notes for anyone re-running this

ESMFold must run on an a100. The esm/2.0.0 module ships torch 1.13.1+cu117, built for sm_37–sm_86. On an ada6000 (sm_89), h100 (sm_90) or blackwell6000 (sm_120) it does not refuse — it warns and returns garbage. One run produced 487 nonsense errors and 72 “successful” models that were equally worthless. bin/esmfold_batch.py now checks the device capability against torch.cuda.get_arch_list() and exits.
exfab cannot run ESMFold or AF3 — its node has only ada6000.
The signalp, esm, predgpi, targetp and dbcanlight modules all activate conda environments via the shell function, so eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)" must precede them.
Reusable intermediates do not belong in $SCRATCH. The DuckDB export, candidate FASTA and MMseqs families were written there once and lost when the job ended; they live in analysis/mucor_secretome/cache/ (gitignored) now and rebuild in under three minutes.
Slurm’s START_TIME for pending jobs here is a pessimistic placeholder, not a forecast.

title: Delta Gain: findings synthesis
text:
One result on this page has since been qualified



Section 5.1 reports that enriched Pfam families show new genomes adding far more novelty than an order-matched baseline null — +14.6 to +14.9 points at 70 % identity, against roughly +0.4 to +2.2 for CAZy, MEROPS and random-Pfam controls. It is the largest effect in the document.
A later test shows that most of that excess is where the genomes were deposited, not what is in them. Two UW-Madison Y1000+ BioProjects contribute 1,033 genomes — 5.8 % of the new side — and they carry about three quarters of the enriched-family novelty. Their assemblies went to GenBank in 2024 but their proteins went to Figshare, so the proteins are public and yet absent from the nr baseline this analysis screens against. Counting them as known turns the enriched families’ +24.8-point excess over the controls into a 23.1-point deficit.
Read the test → The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition
What that test does not do is re-run the order-matched null with those genomes moved into the baseline, so the +14.6 figure below has not been recomputed — it has been shown to rest on a confound. The other family sets are far less affected: the median family loses 86.6 % of its novelty among the enriched families and 0.8 % among the random controls. Sections 3 and 4, which are whole-proteome rather than family-level, are not touched by this.

Source of truth for every number is docs/DELTA_GAIN_PLAN.md (§11 status log) and docs/FAMILY_DIVERSITY_PLAN.md (§10 status table). Scripts are in bin/, launchers in launch/, results under results/ of the delta-gain-fungi working directory (HPCC, /bigdata/stajichlab/shared/projects/BFD/DeltaGain_Fungi). title: Delta Gain: findings synthesis
section: 1. The question and the short answer
text:
1. The question and the short answer

How much NEW protein-level information do newly annotated fungal genomes add, compared with what was already known from previously annotated fungal genomes, controlling for the many re-sequenced strains of the same species?

Baseline = 5,703 genomes with a prior NCBI annotation. New = 17,864 matched genomes without one (183.1 M proteins). About 60 % of new genomes are strains of species already in the baseline.
Short answer.

Whole-proteome view. 50.2 / 29.2 / 22.4 % of new proteins fall in clusters with no baseline member at 95 / 70 / 50 % identity. That protein-weighted headline understates novelty per species and is dominated by heavily resequenced species. Counted once per species about 39 % of proteins are novel at 50 % identity, and the novelty comes from new species and genera, not from new strains.
Strains add little. Strains of baseline species are 60 % of new proteins but 36 % of the novel ones (13.3 % novel at 50 %, median genome 5 %). New species in a baseline genus are 27.6 % novel; new genus or higher 57-63 %.
Most novel proteins are still homologs of known families. Of the survivor clusters seen in 5 or more genomes, 79 % have a detectable baseline homolog by sensitive search; 10.7 % have none. Among all 12.2 M single-genome clusters 63 % have a homolog and 21 % none.
Novel protein mass is species-restricted. 82 % of survivor clusters (61 % of survivor proteins) come from one species.
Within a family, new genomes add about what the same number of baseline genomes would. For typical CAZy, MEROPS, random Pfam and secondary-metabolism backbone families the extra is about 1-3 percentage points. Pfam families chosen for being enriched in new genomes (mostly Saccharomycotina yeast families) show about +15 points, and that replicates in independent species.
Unseen clades are not special. New genomes from orders with no baseline genome are no more novel than a typical held-out baseline order (pooled and class-matched nulls, about -2 points at 70 %).
Artefacts do not explain the result. Predictor mismatch (NCBI vs BFD gene models) adds 1.5-3 points; contamination-flagged genomes supply 8.2 % of novel protein mass; annotated transposons about 1 %; there is no excess of prokaryote-like best hits among novel proteins.
Novel family members are often degenerate or partial. Novel GH18 and S08 regions are shorter and more often miss catalytic residues; novel S08 hits include probable carboxylase false hits. These are not evidence of new catalytic function.
The fungal 50 % cluster pangenome is not saturated. Adding species in random order, each further species still contributes about 2.7-4.5 thousand new clusters. A new species adds about five times more clusters per genome than a resequenced strain of a known species (about 1,870 vs 350).
No secretome or expansion signal. New genomes do not carry more signal peptides or small-secreted-protein candidates than same-order baseline genomes, survivors are not enriched for them, and CAZy/MEROPS copy number changes are small and balanced (19 families expand, 23 contract per 1,000 proteins).
The family result is robust. It does not change with coverage threshold, coverage mode or Pfam region definition (five families, sensitivity run).

2. Design in brief







Element
What was done




Baseline / new
genome_classes.tsv: 5,703 baseline, 17,864 new matched genomes (196 not annotated and 2 ambiguous-tag genomes kept out of headline numbers).


Funnel
Nested MMseqs2 linclust over BASE (NCBI proteins) and NEW (BFD proteins) at 95 % (90 % cov), 70 % and 50 % identity (80 % bidirectional coverage). A new protein is novel at a tier if its cluster has no baseline member. Survivors = novel at 50 %.


Family walk
Regions of a Pfam / CAZy / MEROPS family (or subfamily) from the BFD re-annotation of both groups (no predictor confound), clustered inside the family at 90 / 70 / 50 / 30 %. Novel region = cluster with no baseline member.


Nulls
F3: equally many same-order baseline genomes (baseline-vs-baseline). F3b: leave one whole order out. F3c: class-matched version for orders with no baseline genome. Genome-level and species-collapsed variants, 200 draws.


Controls
Predictor control; rank decomposition; rarefaction to k genomes per species; size-matched random-Pfam control; species-half split-sample test; contamination/TE triage; quality (BUSCO, N50) within-order diagnostics.


Survivor characterisation
Pfam/CAZy/MEROPS labels, taxonomic breadth, sensitive MMseqs2 search (-s 6.0) against the 16.45 M baseline-known tier-50 representatives, profile search of no-hit clusters, Swiss-Prot taxonomy screen, ESMFold pilot.

3.3b Species accumulation of 50 % clusters (E4)
All 23,567 genomes with annotated proteins (237 M distinct genome x tier-50 cluster pairs, 33.4 M clusters) were grouped into species units: 2,778 baseline species, 822 new-genome groups of species that also have a baseline genome (N_known, about 10.7 k mostly resequenced genomes) and 4,632 new species (N_newsp, about 7.2 k genomes). Units were added in random order (20 permutations per ordering) and each cluster was credited to the first unit that contains it (bin/accumulation.py, results/accumulation/; figure figures/E4_accumulation.svg).



Species accumulation



No saturation. The curve is close to linear. After all 2,778 baseline species (16.25 M clusters) each further species still adds about 4.0-4.5 k clusters at the start of the new units (positions 2,776-3,200), declining only to about 2.7 k for the last 230 new species. The 50 % cluster pangenome of the fungal kingdom is open at this sampling depth.
Baseline-first ordering. New units add 17.14 M clusters absent from the baseline (matches the 17.10 M survivor clusters counted independently; the small gap is clusters held only by genomes outside the two classes): 3.72 M from the 822 resequenced-species groups (about 350 clusters per genome) and 13.42 M from the 4,632 new species (about 1,870 clusters per genome). Strains of known species add little per genome; new species add roughly five times more.
New-first ordering (contrast). The first 2,778 random new species cover 13.5 M clusters, 17 % fewer than the 2,778 baseline species (16.2 M). The 5,454 new species together cover 22.2 M clusters, and the baseline still adds 11.2 M clusters after all new genomes (about 4.0 k per baseline species). The baseline therefore carries a large share of sequence space that the new genomes do not reproduce.
Caveat. Baseline proteins are NCBI gene models and new proteins are BFD models, so cluster counts per species include the 1.5-3 point predictor effect and differences in proteome size and completeness; the curves describe species sampling of 50 % clusters, not new families (most clusters are small and lineage-restricted, see section 4).



3.4 Artefact checks

Predictor mismatch. 300 baseline genomes scored as NCBI vs BFD annotations against the same 1,000-genome reference: novel fraction 57.3 -> 60.0 / 34.5 -> 35.8 / 25.7 -> 26.8 % (95 / 70 / 50 %). The gene-model difference inflates novelty by about 1.5-3 points.
Contamination and transposons. Genomes with GC more than 8 points from their order median (1,067) or BUSCO < 50 (322) are 6-7 % of new genomes and give 8.2 % of novel protein mass. Annotated TE domains label about 1 % of survivor proteins.
Horizontal transfer / contamination screen. Best Swiss-Prot hit of survivor representatives (metagenome-bin genomes excluded) is prokaryotic for 4.1-4.8 % of survivors vs 5.2 % of background proteins; at >= 40 % identity 1.0-1.3 % vs 1.3 %. No enrichment. This is a screen only (< 50 % of survivors have a Swiss-Prot hit; no phylogeny).

Secretome. Whole-proteome signal-peptide fraction is 7.64 % in new vs 7.71 % in baseline genomes; small-secreted-protein (SSP) candidates (signal peptide, <= 300 aa, >= 4 Cys, no GPI anchor, no transmembrane helix beyond a signal anchor) are 1.369 % vs 1.359 %. The enriched list is a Saccharomycotina yeast list; BUSCO of those orders is 75-80 %, so this is a lineage effect rather than a quality flag.



5.1b Sensitivity to clustering and region choices (E9)
Five families (GH18, S08, the ketosynthase PF00109, one enriched Pfam PF10450, one random-control Pfam PF01568) were re-clustered and re-nulled (1,010 genomes per side, 200 draws) with later-tier coverage 60 / 80 / 90 %, target-only instead of bidirectional coverage, and Pfam regions by alignment span instead of envelope (Pfam families only; CAZy and MEROPS have one span definition). The 30 % tier is already a default tier. Details: docs/E9_RESULTS.md.

The family-level result is insensitive to these choices. New minus null at 70 %: GH18 +0.010, S08 +0.004, PF00109 0.000, control +0.001, with variants differing from the default by at most 0.004-0.007, far inside the null intervals.
The enriched family keeps its excess in every variant: PF10450 +0.095 to +0.101 at 70 % (intervals exclude 0 in all five variants) and +0.065 to +0.074 at 50 %, so the enrichment is not an artefact of one clustering setting.
The 30 % tier adds no signal: all differences within +-0.02 with intervals spanning 0. Across 15 family x tier cells there is one sign flip, PF10450 at 30 % with alignment-span regions (-0.007 vs +0.018), with every interval spanning 0.

The family-level novelty of new taxa is what sampling any unseen clade gives, not a special property of these genomes. Caveat: only four classes allow the class-matched test, with 5 genomes per draw.


5.3 Where the novelty sits
Novelty is clade-specific, not family-wide: GH18 is 7.0 % novel overall but 2.9 % in Hypocreales and 2.1 % in Eurotiales vs 72.8 % in Ascoideales, 34.4 % in Pichiales and 23.0 % in Boletales; S08 is 5.0 % in Hypocreales vs 31.1 % in Agaricales. 6. Lifestyle correlates
FungalTraits 1.2 genus labels (Põlme et al. 2020) cover 1,061 of 1,204 genera with a new genome (16,085 of 17,865 genomes). Unit = genus; within-order deviation in novel fraction at 50 %, permutation test inside orders. All genomes: mycorrhizal +4.4 points, saprotroph +1.2, plant pathogen -3.9, animal-associated -2.8 (n.s.), yeast growth form -4.1. Holding relatedness fixed, only mycorrhizal remains (+7.5 points among new species in a baseline genus; +2.0 among new genera or higher); plant pathogens stay at -3.0 among distant genomes. Most lifestyle differences are sampling depth and relatedness, and lifestyle is nested in clade, so this is a screen, not a causal result.

title: Delta Gain: findings synthesis
text:
7. Limitations

Baseline definition. “Baseline” is “had a prior NCBI annotation”. It is a sampling, not a knowledge, boundary: the baseline is enriched for model organisms and well-sampled clades.
Strain pseudo-replication. Handled by rarefaction, species-collapsed variants and genus-level units, but any protein-weighted number is dominated by heavily resequenced species.
Predictor. The funnel mixes NCBI baseline proteins with BFD new proteins (1.5-3 points); the family walk uses BFD annotation for both groups and avoids this.
Selection. The enriched Pfam list is selected on the outcome; it is a candidate list, not a genome-wide estimate.
Family nulls only cover orders present in both groups; the clade-matched F3c has few classes.
Labels and searches use cluster representatives; sensitive-search hits indicate homology, not function. No-hit clusters are a mix of orphan genes and gene-model artefacts that this work cannot separate.
Proxies. The HGT screen (Swiss-Prot taxonomy) and the BGC-backbone analysis (domain level) are cheaper stand-ins for a phylogeny-based HGT analysis and for antiSMASH.

title: Fungal pigments: carotenoid, melanin and mycosporine pathways
text:
Status: pre-census chapter. Written 2026-11-21. Code and tables: analysis/pathway_census/.






What this chapter is, what it is not, and where it stops being reliable



This chapter describes the curated knowledge bases for four fungal pigment and pigment-like pathways: carotenoid, DHN melanin, L-DOPA melanin and mycosporine. It describes what each table holds and how strong the evidence is for each step.
It reports no gene counts. The census has not been run on the BFD genomes for any of the four pathways. It waits for the owner’s review of the curated step sets (section 6). Every statement of the form “fungi have X genes” is therefore missing on purpose.
Nothing here was tested at the bench. The curators read PubMed abstracts and database records. They did not read full texts, except where a table says so.
Two evidence readings exist. Under the strict quote rule used in the tables, no carotenoid route and no complete DHN route is above tier T3. Under the alternative context reading, two links (carG, Q9P885; SDH1, P56221) stay at T1a and the route tiers rise. The owner has not chosen between them.
Labels: MEASURED = counted from the committed tables on 2026-11-21. REPORTED = taken from a message of the EBC agent, not re-measured. UNVERIFIED = not checked. General biology that is not in the tables is marked background and was not verified here.




The project began as two chapters for the fungal genome census, carotenoid and melanin biosynthesis, modelled on the earlier peroxygenase (UPO) chapter. Structure and affinity prediction was dropped. Mycosporines and mycosporine-like amino acids (MAAs) were added later because the metabolite corpus (held by the EBC agent) shows MAA library names in marine samples.
The working question was whether a genome that carries a pathway shows its product more often in the metabolite corpus. That comparison failed its pre-set detectability gate and was not run (section 5). The curated tables remain useful on their own as a reference for later census work.



Each pathway has five flat tables in kb/<pathway>/: compound, reaction, reaction_participant, step, step_reaction. A step is a position in the pathway, defined by a protein family (Pfam, TIGRFAM or KO). A step_reaction row links a step to a reaction through one named protein of one named organism, with an evidence tier.







Tier
Meaning




T1a
The fungal enzyme was assayed, or its product was identified after heterologous expression. The quoted abstract sentence must name that protein and state an assay or product


T1b
Gene deletion or complementation with analysis of intermediates in the fungus


T1c
Deletion with a colour phenotype only


T2
Reaction shown for the same enzyme family in another organism


T3
Inferred from family or orthology, or a T1 claim whose quote fails the rule above


T4
Hypothesis with no direct evidence



A route tier that holds only across several organisms is not reported as a tier for any single organism.
An independent script (bin/verify_kb.py) re-fetches each accession, gene name, PubMed identifier, quoted sentence, sequence hash, ChEBI or PubChem identifier and formula, and checks them against the files. MEASURED result: 1,677 checks, 1,647 pass, 6 fail, 24 unchecked (kb/VERIFICATION_REPORT.md). A pass means the public record agrees with the file. It does not mean the biology is right.

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
What this is



A working analysis, not a finished study. Every clade call, site call and candidate here is a prediction from sequence and structure; no enzyme in this report has been expressed or assayed by us. Section 7 states the limitations and section 4 reports the results that came out negative, including four attempts to extend the model that failed their own tests.
The report is explicit about where it stops: identifying PF01328 sites is validated (95/95 against the published structure-based matrix), ranking clade-V-like pockets is reliable for ordering candidates, and predicting whether an arbitrary protein is an active peroxygenase is not reliable (out-of-clade AUC 0.556). Section 3 explains why that is arithmetic rather than something reanalysis can fix.
The source of truth is analysis/enzymes_UPO/ in the repository; this page renders REPORT.md from that directory, so the two cannot drift. The 45 documents it synthesizes are listed at the end, and the per-protein table it describes is in the repository beside the code that built it.
What exists, what can be called reliably, and what cannot.
2026-11-15. A synthesis of the UPO workstream. Every number here is produced by code in this directory and stated with its own evidence document; where a result is negative or bounded, the bound is given rather than the headline. The documents this draws on are listed at the end, and the per-document detail is the authority — this page is the route through them.
Unspecific peroxygenases (UPOs, Pfam PF01328) are secreted fungal heme-thiolate enzymes that transfer oxygen from H₂O₂ to unactivated C–H bonds. They do with a single cheap co-substrate what P450 monooxygenases need a reductase and NAD(P)H for, which is why they are of interest for synthesis. Fewer than thirty have been characterized biochemically.

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
In short

The family is large and the catalytic machinery is common. 97,520 PF01328 proteins in 15,137 genomes; 34,561 (35.4 %) carry the full catalytic core.
Almost none of it is sequence-novel, and the apparent novelty is a deposition artefact. All 7,055 representatives have an nr hit. Apparent novelty is 2.0 % for RefSeq-annotated genomes and 18.7 % for GenBank-only ones (z = 7.4).
What is genuinely new is lineage coverage, not sequence. Whole well-supported clades of UPO-like proteins contain no characterized enzyme at all.
Active-site identification is reliable; activity prediction outside clade V is not. 95/95 agreement on site assignment against the published structure-based matrix; out-of-clade AUC 0.556 — chance — on predicting activity.
The clade caller refuses most of the database, by design. 78.9 % unassigned; 10.7 % carry a reliable call. Two independent callers agree 99.6 % above the trust boundary and 78.1 % below it.
Four attempts to break the ceiling all failed, and each failure was measured. Reference expansion made precision worse (80 % → 66 %); applicability distance failed as a confidence measure (p = 0.88); structural features from predicted models made the activity model worse (0.333); the Boltz-2 run hit its pre-declared kill switch and its 14 models were discarded.
Everything traces to one number: 19 characterized enzymes, three of five clades having one or two.
Two errors were found in BFD itself while building the candidate list — one of them affecting every consumer of the gene-model flags.

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
2. Novelty is deposition, not biology
The workstream began as “are there new UPOs in early-diverging fungi?” The answer is largely no, and the way it is no is the interesting part.
Every one of the 7,055 catalytic-core representatives has a hit in nr. The apparent 18 % novelty splits cleanly by where the source genome was deposited: 2.0 % for genomes with a RefSeq (GCF_) annotation against 18.7 % for GenBank-only genomes, z = 7.4. A protein looks new when its genome’s proteins were never deposited in a form nr indexes.
This is the same effect, in a different family, as the one measured for the delta-gain funnel’s enriched-Pfam result, where counting the Y1000+ yeast genomes as public removes three quarters of the novelty (analysis/delta_gain_funnel/REPORT.md). Two independent analyses in this repository now put a number on the same confound.
Contamination was checked and is not the explanation: UPO genes sit on contigs more gene-rich than their genome’s typical contig (G1_FINDINGS.md §6).
What is new is lineage coverage. Several well-supported clades hold thousands of UPO-like proteins and not one characterized enzyme. That is what the candidate list targets.

3. Calling clades: a caller that refuses
The production clade call is phylogenetic placement (EPA) on a 187-leaf reference tree built in-house from Zamocky et al. 2022, not nearest-neighbour identity to the 19 characterized enzymes. It replaced the earlier caller after direct comparison (RECONCILIATION.md §1).



Figure 1. The 187-leaf UPO reference tree.


Maximum likelihood (IQ-TREE, Q.PFAM+R7), rooted on Mucorales. Coloured sectors are Zamocky et al. 2022’s lineages; the black arcs outside them are Clades I–V with SH-aLRT/UFBoot support. The 19 named tips are every characterized enzyme the field has. Note how few they are, and how unevenly they fall — Clades III and V hold most of them, Clades I and II almost none. That imbalance is the origin of every limit in this report. PDF

The 78.9 % is the caller declining, not failing. PF01328 is wider than the UPO clades, so most of these proteins are not expected to belong to any of them.
An external check on where the boundary sits. The table carries two clade calls made by methods that are not derived from each other — EPA placement and nearest-reference identity. They agree on 99.6 % of reliable rows and 78.1 % of extrapolated rows. The methods converge above the boundary and diverge below it, measured on real BFD proteins rather than on references. This does not show the calls are correct — two methods can agree and both be wrong, and both rest on the same 19 enzymes — only that the boundary drawn from reference tests reproduces on data.



Figure 4. Matched-identity validation of both callers on the 19 characterized enzymes.


Each enzyme is re-called with every reference above an identity ceiling removed, so the test asks what happens at a given distance from anything known. Upper panel: precision when the caller commits, with exact binomial 95 % CI and correct/committed counts. Lower panel: how often it declines. The 187-leaf caller (blue) is 16/16, 13/13, 4/4 and 14/14 — it does not make a wrong call at any distance — while the 19-reference caller (orange) falls to 3/8 at 45–55 % identity. The intervals are wide because n = 19; this shows the caller abstains rather than guesses, not that it is accurate to within a few percent. PDF

Reading Table T1 without being misled
figures/data/table_T1.md gives per-clade references, support, BFD membership, catalytic core, Glu180 frequency and measured activity range. Its “BFD proteins” column and the tier table above count different things: Table T1 assigns every protein to its best placement regardless of confidence, so it partitions all 97,520, while the tier table applies the 0.5 threshold. Clade I shows 41,679 in one and 2,565 in the other for that reason. Clade I is also the same group as Zamocky’s Basidiomycetous 3rd (Family II, long).
Three caveats travel with that table and should not be separated from it:

The glomeromycete clade’s 784 members are not 784 glomeromycete UPOs. Only 121 are Glomeromycota; 360 are Dothideomycetes, and 585 of the 663 outsiders carry long_pendant. Report it as 121 plus 78 short-pendant others.
Basidiomycetous 1st holds ~2,265 ascomycete proteins that are not long-pendant — see §6.
Family I (short) has low node support (SH-aLRT/UFBoot 79.4/65); Clades III–V sit inside it.

Flows are coloured by how much the old call could be trusted. Calls made inside the validated identity range (blue) mostly survive; extrapolated Clade III and V calls (orange) largely move to Clade IV or II, or leave Clades I–V altogether. The Boltz-2 run and its kill switch. The plan declared in advance that if predicted channel widths failed to reproduce the five experimental ones, the other 14 models would be discarded. They failed. The 14 models were discarded and the conclusion recorded is that this cannot be done with predicted structures at this scale.
The channel-width question, with its reversals recorded. CAVER 3.0.2 gave ~1 Å bottlenecks and the first conclusion was that the ring rule does not transfer. Adding the fifth structure (TteUPO, 9IZ8 — the widest channel measured, zero activity) dropped it to r = +0.452. text:
5. What to assay
Three lists, answering different questions. They can be run together.
37 lineage candidates (CANDIDATES.md) — rules written and committed before the selection was run, in 8 pools across clade IV and six uncharacterized lineages, one protein per genus, one per 70 % identity cluster. A result in pool A or B is a first measurement for a lineage. Suggested first set: 12. Pool C (Glu180 absent — the lineage trait itself) waits on the structure question.
A 96-protein panel (ASSAY_PANEL.md) — 84 predicted active, 12 predicted inactive controls, 61 distinct pocket 5-mers, 79 species, 16 lineages, 93 % outside clade V. The controls are the point: GmaUPO-II shows the predicted-inactive cell is exactly where the model is known to fail, so assaying only predicted positives would measure precision and leave the false-negative rate unknown.
Six pre-registered external predictions (EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.md) — the cheapest experiment that would settle the model question. Six characterized UPOs already exist as purified enzymes elsewhere with no published 4-propylguaiacol number. Predictions recorded before any measurement: active DchUPO, DcaUPO; inactive CraUPO, MweUPO, PabUPO-II, UPO1_Codo. A failure among the predicted actives is the informative outcome — it would confirm the rule overcalls outside clade V, which is what the 0.556 warns about.
Decision D1 (Eurotiales sourcing for the Pichia construct) is recorded as moot: it rested on the pocket score, which does not predict anything of interest outside clade V (PLAN.md).

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
6. Two errors found in BFD
Both were found while building the candidate list, and both are recorded for BFD rather than worked around here (bfd_findings/REPORT.md).
Start/stop-codon flags are wrong, database-wide. The shortlist’s gene-model rule removed Mucorales and Glomeromycota proteins wholesale (83 % and 75 % flagged incomplete). They are not incomplete. Splicing 5,816 models from the assemblies showed 99.3 % of flagged-missing starts and 99.8 % of flagged-missing stops are present; the true incomplete rate is ~0.2 %, not 10–60 %. The cause is case-sensitive codon matching against soft-masked genomes — a lower-case atg read as absent — which is why TAA stops are flagged missing more often (39.8 %) than TAG (18.8 %) or TGA (16.1 %). Fixed in Fungi_BFD fb1d7cd; gene_transcripts.parquet predates the fix. Any consumer that filtered on these flags silently dropped ~10 % of models BFD-wide and about half in Mucorales and Glomeromycota.
An ascomycete lineage inside a basidiomycete clade. 2,265 of the 6,378 members of Basidiomycetous 1st are Ascomycota, in 2,190 genomes — almost all single-copy, in 47.5 % of Dothideomycetes and all 67 Orbiliomycetes genomes, attaching as close to the references as the clade’s basidiomycete members and carrying the clade’s Asn180 at the same frequency (87.4 %). Zamocky noted one ascomycete transfer into this clade; this is two orders of magnitude more. Spread across thousands of independent genomes at single copy, it is not contamination, and it is not one recent transfer. It fits an old ascomycete UPO lineage. Placement cannot decide between nested (transfer) and sister (old lineage) because the reference holds only the basidiomycete diversity. The test that would settle it — an ML tree of ~150 + ~150 dereplicated members with two outgroups — is specified and not done.

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
7. Limitations

Nineteen characterized enzymes. Three of five clades have one or two. 71 of 114 matched-identity test cases were impossible because removing a reference’s close relatives removed its whole clade.
One substrate, one assay, one publication. Task B’s calibration is 4-propylguaiacol conversion. It says nothing about which rings an enzyme cleaves — that is a separate measured negative.
Clade calls below ~55 % identity are not trustworthy under the old caller (precision 38 %), and BFD’s median identity to a reference is 43.8 %. The placement caller made no errors at matched identity down to <35 %, but on 19 enzymes.
69.6 % of BFD falls outside the calibration domain, and calib_domain is coverage, not confidence — it was tested as a confidence measure and failed.
No assay supports any rate or substrate range for any BFD protein here. catalytic_core means four residues are present: necessary, not sufficient.
Clade IV has one characterized member, so every clade IV row stays flagged +provisional_cladeIV; and clade IV’s status as a separate clade is unresolved (20–28 % bootstrap) even though the group is real (652/789 confirmed).
The shortlist should be re-run once the BFD tables are rebuilt; pools B4 and B5 were drawn from an eligible set shrunk by the flag bug. The 37 picks themselves stand.

title: Unspecific peroxygenases across 15,137 fungal genomes
text:
8. What would change this
More characterized enzymes. Every limit above traces to 19, and the alternatives were tested rather than assumed: expansion with inferred labels makes the caller worse, the structural route is calibrated on four, a second 4-PG panel does not exist, and labels from other papers are invalid because they are substrate-specific — PaDa-I, the field’s benchmark peroxygenase, converts 4-propylguaiacol at 1.7 %.
The six pre-registered assays are the cheapest move. The 96-well panel is the thorough one.

title: The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition
text:
What this is



A single targeted test, not a new analysis of the funnel. It asks one question of the funnel’s largest family-level effect — the enriched Pfam families’ +14.6-point excess over an order-matched null — and answers it by joining the existing cluster tables against NCBI BioProject metadata.
It is a companion to the funnel findings, which reports that effect in section 5.1. Read that page’s qualification box first if you have not.
The source of truth is analysis/delta_gain_funnel/ in this repository — code, tests, SLURM driver and the per-family output tables that the numbers below are computed from. This page renders REPORT.md from that directory, so the two cannot drift.
The report is explicit that it does not recompute the +14.6-point figure: doing that needs the order-matched null re-run with the Y1000+ genomes moved into the baseline, which has not been done. It shows the figure rests on a confound, which is a different claim.
2026-11-15. Code in analysis/delta_gain_funnel/bin/y1000_join.py, driver slurm/y1000_join.sh (job 32102558, 1 min 20 s), tests in test/ (17 passing). Per-family results in out/y1000_enriched.tsv and out/y1000_control.tsv.

title: The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition
text:
The question
The delta-gain funnel’s largest family-level result is that Pfam families chosen for being enriched in new genomes carry +14.6 to +14.9 points more novel clusters than an order-matched baseline null, against +2.2 for size-matched random Pfam controls. The funnel’s own notes observe that the enriched list “is a Saccharomycotina yeast list” and read this as a lineage effect, supported by the fact that it replicates when the list is selected on one half of the species and evaluated on the other.
The objection the split-sample test does not answer: replication across species does not distinguish new biology from a shared deposition history. “Baseline” in the funnel means “had a prior NCBI annotation”. That is a boundary around a database, not around knowledge. A sequencing project that deposits assemblies to GenBank unannotated and releases its own proteomes elsewhere puts every one of its genomes on the new side, however long its proteins have been public — and it does so for all of its species at once, so a split-sample test replicates it perfectly.

title: The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition
section: What this does and does not establish
text:
What this does and does not establish

It is not a recomputation of the +14.6-point figure. That statistic is a comparison against an order-matched baseline null with its own resampling; this is the raw novel-cluster share under two definitions of “known”. The direction and size are not in doubt, but the published number should be recomputed properly by re-running the order-matched null with Y1000+ in the baseline, not adjusted by hand from this table.
It covers 401 Pfam families, not the corpus. The funnel’s genome-wide figures (50.2 / 29.2 / 22.4 % novel at 95/70/50 %) are untouched by this run. Y1000+ is 5.8 % of the new-side genomes here, and its species are nearly all distinct, so some effect on the genome-wide numbers is likely — it has not been measured.
It does not show the enriched families are uninteresting. Yeast-specific families that Y1000+ sampled deeply are real biology; the claim it undercuts is that the funnel’s database comparison discovered them.
Y1000+ is the largest such project, not the only one. Any project depositing assemblies without annotation has the same effect. The same join against other large unannotated submissions would say whether this is one project or a general pattern, and that has not been run.

title: The enriched-Pfam signal is mostly Y1000+ deposition
text:
Consequence for the funnel
The funnel’s limitations already state that baseline is “a sampling, not a knowledge boundary” and that the enriched list “is selected on the outcome; it is a candidate list, not a genome-wide estimate.” Both are correct and both are now quantified: for this result the sampling boundary accounts for three quarters of it.
The honest summary of the enriched-Pfam result is that it measures where Saccharomycotina genomes were deposited, and that the lineage reading is not supported once deposition is controlled for. It should not be published as a novelty finding in its present form.

section: 7. How to connect this corpus to other data
text:
7. How to connect this corpus to other data

The unit is the accession, not the group. Hold out whole accessions. Collapse the 174 mirrored duplicate groups first (REPORTED).
Stratify by instrument and polarity. Orbitrap positive is the primary stratum. Orbitrap negative and qTOF positive are reported separately only when a cell has at least 6 capable and 30 non-capable accessions (PROPOSED).
Separate yeast from filamentous fungi. Capability, growth form and extraction method are confounded.
Drop genus-only “Fungi” groups (15 of 116).
Define “observed” two ways and report both: library name, and accepted formula plus MS2 class. Formula alone is MSI level 4 at best.
Never match on mass alone. Isobars exist (palythene and usujirene share m/z 285.14; mycosporine-methylamine-threonine and mycosporine glutaminol share 303.154).
Library labels need care. 21.5% of hits are NIST14 spectral-match labels. Two MAA-named groups with a fungal dominant taxon hold non-fungal runs, so the hit cannot be assigned to the fungus.
Run the gate first. Get the detectability counts before building a model. This saved a full comparison here.
Run any SIRIUS comparison with a matched control set processed the same way.
Keep evidence tiers attached to claims. A T3 link is an annotation, not an assay. A route tier that holds only across several organisms is not a tier for any one organism.
Identifiers: KEGG ids are cross-references only (academic licence). ChEBI and PubChem licences for a shared table are UNVERIFIED. Release outside the group is an open owner decision.
Genome gaps: BFD holds fungi only. Bacterial, algal, plant and animal producers need genomes from elsewhere.

8. What would change these conclusions

A compound with at least 6 capable and 3 observing accessions in the primary stratum, and a positive control at 3 accessions, would open M2 for that compound.
Metabolomics of fungi grown for a pigment (induced carotenoid or melanin conditions, targeted extraction) would test H1 and H2 directly. This is outside the corpus.
A matched negative-control SIRIUS run would decide whether class anchors (M3) mean anything.
Fungal genomes with confirmed MAA genes, once Task 6 finishes, would let the marine signal be compared with a fungal capability call.
